title: Generative Refinement for Low-Budget Black-Box Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2607.00691v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Black-box optimization is a fundamental tool in science and engineering for optimizing objectives when gradient information is unavailable. It becomes especially difficult when the objective function is expensive to evaluate, limiting the evaluation budget to a few tens or hundreds of queries, and when good solutions occupy complex, low-measure regions of the search space. Generative models can supply useful structural priors in such settings, but existing generative BBO approaches bring significant evaluation cost. We identify three design principles for generative optimization under such low-budget conditions: avoid objective learning, optimize in candidate space, and make every evaluation count. Together, these principles motivate separating structural modeling from objective-driven search. translated_title: 面向低预算黑盒优化的生成式精细化方法
translated_abstract: 黑盒优化是科学和工程领域中在梯度信息不可用时优化目标函数的基本工具。当目标函数的评估代价高昂（将评估预算限制在几十到几百次查询），且优质解占据搜索空间中复杂、低测度的区域时，该问题变得尤为困难。生成模型在此类场景中可以提供有用的结构先验，但现有的生成式黑盒优化（BBO）方法会带来显著的评估成本。我们为这种低预算条件下的生成式优化确定了三条设计原则：避免目标函数学习、在候选空间中进行优化、以及让每一次评估都发挥价值。这些原则共同促使我们将结构建模与目标驱动搜索相分离。我们将这些原则实例化于SPARROW——一个简单的序列优化器，它维护一个持久化、按优劣排序的已评估候选解存档，并使用一个……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文针对评估预算极低的黑盒优化场景提出三条设计原则（避免目标学习、在候选空间中优化、珍惜每次评估），并据此构建了简单序列优化器SPARROW，通过维护持久化排序的候选解存档，将结构建模与目标驱动搜索分离，从而在极低评估预算下实现高效的生成式优化。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes three design principles for low-budget black-box optimization—avoid objective learning, optimize in candidate space, and make every evaluation count—and instantiates them in SPARROW, a simple sequential optimizer that maintains a persistent, ranked archive of evaluated candidates to separate structural modeling from objective-driven search.
